headline_marked: [[Google Disables Search]] in schools that reject its AI tools
headline: Google Disables Search in schools that reject its AI tools
summary: Students in schools that reject Google's AI features will lose access to Search, with administrators unable to toggle them separately.
details: Google is completely disabling Search in K-12 schools that reject its AI features, such as Gemini and Gemini Notebook. The company stated that these AI tools, along with Google Search, will be entirely off for student accounts unless administrators explicitly enable them.

Administrators face a difficult choice: enabling Google's AI features means keeping Search accessible, but they cannot disable the AI tools without also losing Search functionality. Google's vice president of education, Chris Phillips, explained that 'Search and AI are deeply integrated.'

This move comes after Google began turning on AI features by default in Google Classroom, which is used by over 150 million students and teachers globally. The decision has raised concerns among lawmakers and educators about the potential impact of AI on students' learning abilities and test scores.

Google is also working to address concerns about students using AI for 'shortcuts.' The company is testing a new Guided Learning feature, designed to help students work through problems, within its AI Overviews in Search, starting this month in select US schools.

headline_marked: Windows 11 [[8GB RAM PCs get up to 40% faster]] with new optimizations
headline: Windows 11 8GB RAM PCs get up to 40% faster with new optimizations
summary: Microsoft claims new software updates make Windows 11 up to 20% more responsive and multitasking up to 40% faster on machines with only 8GB of RAM.
details: Microsoft has announced performance improvements for Windows 11 on PCs equipped with 8GB of RAM. This comes as a response to the ongoing component shortage, which has led to manufacturers reducing RAM configurations in new devices.

The company claims Windows is now 20% more responsive and multitasking is 40% faster in lab tests. These optimizations are part of Microsoft's commitment to improving Windows 11's performance, a frequent user complaint since its launch.

Microsoft has implemented a three-pronged approach: better memory utilization, protection of instant interactions, and reduced memory usage by key apps and Windows itself. While 16GB or 32GB RAM configurations are still recommended for optimal performance, these updates aim to enhance the experience on lower-spec machines.

Responsiveness improvements, claimed at 20%, apply to tasks like opening the Start menu, searching, and using File Explorer. Microsoft achieved this by reducing background tasks during active PC use. Edge browser startup times are also reportedly up to 33% faster.

The 40% multitasking speed boost is based on a demanding scenario involving 20 Edge tabs, 4K video playback, large Office files, Outlook, and File Explorer running simultaneously. Microsoft has also reduced the memory footprint of apps like Edge and Microsoft 365 by up to 900MB.
